items.title: India valuations hit 6-year low, but stocks still expensive than EM peers
items.description: India's equity valuations have reached their lowest levels in six years after a recent market decline. Factors contributing to this decline include foreign selling, a weaker rupee, and rising crude prices. Despite lower valuations, overseas investors remain hesitant to invest in Indian equities due to comparative valuations. The MSCI India Index trades at a premium compared to other emerging markets, influencing foreign investor sentiment.

items.title: Stocks in news: Infosys, Kotak Mahindra Bank, YES Bank, Raymond, BPCL, Coforge and Senco Gold
items.description: Indian equity markets have faced a decline for four consecutive sessions, with the Nifty falling significantly. Various factors, including selling by foreign investors and rising crude oil prices, have contributed to this downturn. Notable stocks such as Infosys and Kotak Mahindra Bank have attracted investor attention due to their quarterly earnings. Upcoming developments may influence market sentiment further as investors remain watchful.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Benchmark indices experienced a decline on Friday due to high Brent crude oil prices and global market weakness. Nifty was noted to face immediate resistance at 22,850 levels, with previous week's high acting as a hurdle. The rupee fell against the dollar for the second consecutive day, impacted by rising crude prices. Foreign portfolio investors were net buyers, while domestic institutional investors also increased their holdings.

items.title: BlackRock stays cautious on Indian equities despite cheaper valuations
items.description: BlackRock Investment Institute has not yet adopted a bullish stance on Indian equities due to ongoing uncertainties. The firm anticipates greater clarity on corporate earnings and energy prices before changing its outlook. Despite elevated energy costs, India's economic resilience remains noteworthy amidst geopolitical tensions. Foreign investors have been net sellers of Indian equities for several months, impacting market performance.

items.title: Nifty outlook bearish, but near-term recovery in sight: Analysts
items.description: The Nifty index fell over 2% amid sustained selling pressures with technical indicators signaling support levels. Analysts have identified crucial resistance levels and potential near-term recovery points for the index. Several stocks have shown strength and recommendations have been made for buying opportunities. Additionally, bearish momentum remains evident in specific sectors while futures strategies are advised. Overall, investors are encouraged to adopt a cautious approach during this volatile period.

items.title: Stock Radar: TVS Motor takes support above 200-DMA in October. What should investors do?
items.description: TVS Motor shares are showing signs of recovery after finding support near the 200-DMA. Motilal Oswal’s Shivangi Sarada sees potential upside to Rs 4,500 in the next 3-4 weeks, with Rs 3,900 as the key stop-loss level.

items.title: Tonbo Imaging shares soar another 17% after a 64% listing pop. Buy, sell or hold the stock?
items.description: Tonbo Imaging shares rallied after a strong stock market debut, following heavy demand for its IPO. Investors will track revenue growth, order execution, profitability, working capital and cash flows to assess the defence electronics company’s long-term prospects.

items.title: $7.7 trillion AI bet: Can hyperscalers earn enough to justify the spending?
items.description: Six major hyperscalers are projected to spend $7.7 trillion on AI between 2026 and 2030, but generating adequate returns will be a challenge. UBS estimates they need $1 trillion in additional earnings before interest and taxes by 2031. The key questions are whether AI boosts productivity and companies can monetise those gains.

items.title: Tech picks: Anand Rathi, Cyient among 5 stocks to buy for up to 18% returns in short term
items.description: Markets witnessed a sharp correction during the holiday shortened trading week, with benchmark indices declining in each of the four sessions amid geopolitical concerns and heightened uncertainty. The sustained weakness indicates that the previous week’s recovery has lost momentum, with investors becoming increasingly selective amid global uncertainties and the ongoing corporate earnings season. Corporate earnings will remain a key driver, with TVS Motor, Asian Paints, Trent, Sun Pharma, Bharat Electronics, Indian Oil, Bank of Baroda and GAIL India, among others, scheduled to announce their results.

items.title: Bharat Coking Coal shares rally 5% after Q2 profit turnaround; revenue jumps 39% YoY
items.description: Bharat Coking Coal shares sharply on Monday after the Coal India subsidiary reported a turnaround to profit in Q2 FY27, with net profit at Rs 123.7 crore and revenue up 39% year-on-year to Rs 4,412.58 crore. However, first-half production declined, while technical indicators pointed to continued weakness in the stock.

items.title: Sensex rises 200 pts, Nifty above 22,600 as market snaps 4-day losing streak. Is the relief rally sustainable?
items.description: Indian benchmark indices staged a sharp recovery from early losses, supported by gains in metal, pharmaceutical and select banking stocks. Despite improving market breadth, analysts remained cautious amid elevated crude oil prices, rising volatility and continued weakness in the broader market.

items.title: AU Small Finance Bank shares tumble 10% after Q2 results, but Jefferies and Motilal see up to 37% upside
items.description: AU Small Finance Bank shares fell up to 10% despite a 53% year-on-year rise in Q2 net profit. Jefferies and Motilal Oswal retained Buy ratings, citing growth prospects, improving asset quality and lower credit costs.

items.title: Shriram Finance shares crash 6% as Jefferies, Citi, and other brokerages slash target prices after Q2 results. Why do they still say ‘Buy’?
items.description: Shriram Finance shares fell sharply on Monday after Jefferies, Citi and Motilal Oswal cut their target prices following the NBFC’s Q2 results. Despite concerns over rising credit costs and rural stress, all three brokerages retained their ‘Buy’ ratings, citing strong net interest income, resilient margins and long-term growth potential.

items.title: Paras Healthcare allotment likely today: Check GMP, key details and how to check status
items.description: Paras Healthcare IPO allotment is expected to be finalised today after the Rs 1,450-crore issue was subscribed 2.23 times. With the GMP indicating a potential listing gain of around 1%, investors can check their allotment status on the MUFG Intime, NSE and BSE websites. The hospital chain is scheduled to list on October 28, 2026, after reporting a return to profitability in FY26.

items.title: Coforge slips 3% even as Jefferies, Nomura, others raise targets after Q2 earnings. Why are they bullish?
items.description: Coforge shares fell despite strong Q2 results and brokerages raising target prices. Net profit surged 56.5% year-on-year to Rs 588.1 crore, while revenue jumped 54% to Rs 6,170.8 crore. EBITDA rose 67% to Rs 1,269.7 crore, with margins expanding 168 basis points to 20.6%. The company raised its FY27 EBIT margin guidance to 16%, while its 12-month order book grew 45% to $2.38 billion.

items.title: Infosys shares fall 4% after IT major lowers FY27 guidance. What are Goldman Sachs, Nomura, others saying?
items.description: Infosys shares fell sharply on Monday after the IT major cut its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1-2% from 1.5-3%, citing pricing pressure and a challenging demand environment. While Nomura remains bullish, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Citi and Choice Institutional Equities flag growth concerns, with differing ratings and target prices.

items.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank shares climb 4% after Q2 results. What are Jefferies, Goldman Sachs saying?
items.description: Kotak Mahindra Bank reported strong Q2FY27 earnings, with consolidated profit rising 26% year-on-year. Jefferies, Goldman Sachs, Motilal Oswal and Nuvama maintained Buy ratings, citing growth prospects and improving earnings outlook.

items.title: IndusInd Bank shares rise 2% after Q2 results. Why Jefferies cut target price despite lender swinging to profit
items.description: IndusInd Bank announced a net profit of Rs 1,176 crore for the quarter ending September 2027. The bank's asset quality improved with gross non-performing assets declining to 2.73% from 3.6% a year earlier. Jefferies adjusted its target price for the bank's shares down to Rs 1,130 due to changing credit cost expectations. Motilal Oswal maintained a neutral stance with a target price of Rs 1,050, indicating a positive outlook.

items.title: Nifty's PEG ratio near 10-year low but why don't stocks look cheap yet? Valuation paradox explained
items.description: Nifty’s PEG ratio approaches a decade low, suggesting an enticing potential for valuation and earnings growth. The substantial drop in the forward P/E ratio has heightened hopes for a market recovery. However, rising bond yields and potential earnings downgrades pose challenges to investor sentiment. Selective opportunities arise across sectors, influenced by enhanced credit growth and evolving demand.

items.title: Top Nifty50 stocks analysts suggest buying in this volatile week

The simple average of the above-mentioned five component ratings is normally distributed to reach an average score.

items.title: FSN E-Commerce Ventures among 5 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of October 23, five stocks in the NSE F&O segment recorded a rise of more than 7% in futures open interest compared with the previous trading session, according to StockEdge F&O scan data. A notable increase in futures open interest indicates a substantial rise in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a security. This may reflect market participants initiating new positions or increasing the size of their existing positions.

items.title: Ipca Laboratories among 4 stocks showing RSI trending up
items.description: On October 23, four stocks in the Nifty 500 pack were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.An RSI Trending Up signal occurs when the Relative Strength Index (RSI) crosses above 50 from below, indicating strengthening momentum. RSI is a technical indicator commonly used by traders to assess price momentum and trend strength.

items.title: Yes Bank among 6 stocks to hit 52-week lows and fall up to 32% in a month
items.description: On Monday, the benchmark Sensex rose 483 points to close at 73,606. Despite the broader market gains, six stocks from the BSE 100 index touched fresh 52-week lows, marking their lowest price levels in the past year. A 52-week low represents the lowest price at which a stock has traded over the preceding 12 months and serves as an indicator of its recent price performance.

items.title: Market wrap: Dr Reddys, JSW Steel, Shriram Finance, Tata Consumer top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Monday
items.description: Indian equity markets snapped a four-day losing streak as Sensex and Nifty rebounded, supported by broad-based buying. Dr Reddy’s and JSW Steel led gainers, while rising India VIX signalled continued volatility and technical concerns about downside risks.

items.title: Global Market: European shares flat as investors assess earnings, France turmoil
items.description: European shares traded flat as investors weighed corporate earnings and political uncertainty in France. Falling oil prices, driven by hopes of easing US-Iran tensions, supported travel and leisure stocks, while energy shares declined.

items.title: Ather Energy shares skyrocket 19% after EV maker swings to Rs 1.26 crore profit in Q2
items.description: Ather Energy shares surged nearly 19% after the electric two-wheeler maker reported a net profit of Rs 1.26 crore in Q2 FY27, reversing a loss of Rs 154 crore a year earlier. Revenue rose 62.8% year-on-year to Rs 1,464 crore, while the company also approved Rs 122 crore in capacity expansion.

items.title: SoftBank sells 1.21 crore Ola Electric rights entitlements as EV maker seeks to raise Rs 1,000 crore
items.description: SoftBank sold nearly 28% of its Ola Electric rights entitlements over two sessions as the company launched a Rs 1,000-crore rights issue. Meanwhile, Motilal Oswal entities applied for 2.39 crore shares amid declining revenue and persistent losses.

items.title: Michael Burry's top 10 life lessons for GenZ: 'Buy half the house you can afford'
items.description: Michael Burry provides life advice and personal finance tips to a 26-year-old in a Substack post. He emphasizes the importance of exercising, learning, and relationships while advising against gambling. Burry suggests that individuals should invest wisely, specifically recommending to buy half a house they can afford. He warns about the potential for an AI market crash, predicting possible disappointments in revenue.

items.title: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 30% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: When the profit a company is expected to earn gets marked down, the price the market will pay for its stock has to come down too. That has not quite happened, which is why valuations are still high in many parts of the market. So, don’t assume all the damage is already done just because the market has had a few bad days.

items.title: FIIs raise stakes after two quarters of cuts; 8 stocks rally up to 135% in 3 months
items.description: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) turned net buyers in select stocks during the September 2026 quarter after reducing their exposure for two consecutive quarters. They increased their stakes in 125 stocks with a market capitalisation of over Rs 2,500 crore, following periods of reduced exposure in the December 2025–March 2026 and March–June 2026 quarters.In terms of stock performance, around 15 of these stocks delivered double-digit price returns over the past three months. Among them, the top eight gainers recorded returns ranging from 20% to 135% during the period. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Swiggy shares jump 5% a day after Q2 results sparked a 17% crash. Why brokerages remain bullish despite target price cuts
items.description: Swiggy shares rebounded nearly 5% after plunging 17% following its Q2FY27 results. While food delivery profitability improved, widening Instamart losses prompted Jefferies and Nomura to cut target prices, even as brokerages retained bullish ratings.

items.title: BSE shares jump over 4% as Motilal Oswal upgrades stock to Buy. 4 reasons behind bullish call
items.description: BSE shares rose sharply on Monday after Motilal Oswal upgraded the stock to Buy with a target price of Rs 4,000, implying 23% upside. The brokerage expects strong derivatives volumes, rising premium turnover, improving cash market participation and operating leverage to drive revenue growth, margin expansion and a 27% profit CAGR through FY28.

items.title: Apollo Micro Systems shares rally 9% as Q2 net profit jumps 56% YoY
items.description: Apollo Micro Systems has reported an impressive rise in Q2 earnings, with net profit soaring by 56% compared to last year. Revenues spiked 72%, hitting a milestone of Rs 388 crore for the September quarter. The notable increase in EBITDA showcases solid operational efficiency in the defence sector. The company is dedicated to enhancing its capabilities and expanding into global markets, demonstrating a strategic focus on its future objectives.

items.title: What Bitcoin ETF flows reveal about institutional confidence
items.description: US spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded volatile inflows and outflows, reflecting uneven investor conviction. Although demand recovered during the third quarter, ETF flows have largely followed Bitcoin’s price movements rather than predicted them, making sustained trends more significant than daily fluctuations.

items.title: These large-caps have ‘strong buy’ & ‘buy’ recos and an upside potential of over 25%, according to analysts
items.description: At this juncture, what companies say about their Q2 results, and their outlook for Q3 and Q4, matters a great deal – but only to a certain extent. A company can plan only for what is in its control. No management can predict what the US President will decide, or which way the trouble in the Gulf will turn next.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Tuesday
items.description: Indian stock markets saw a notable recovery after early losses on Monday. Sensex rose nearly 483 points, while Nifty gained over 153 points during the trading session. This rebound followed a four-day decline that significantly impacted investor wealth. Analysts noted value buying supported the recovery, particularly in sectors like power, healthcare, and metals. Despite this, caution prevailed due to geopolitical uncertainties and upcoming policy decisions from major global banks.

items.title: Indian Overseas Bank to raise $500 million as Q2 profit jumps 56%
items.description: Indian Overseas Bank plans to raise $500 million through external commercial borrowings in two tranches by December. The lender reported a 56% rise in Q2 net profit to Rs 1,912 crore, alongside stronger credit growth and improved asset quality.

items.title: The Rs 1.5 lakh crore MTF problem: How shrinking leveraged positions are deepening India's smallcap sell-off
items.description: India’s smallcap sell-off is intensifying as margin trading facility (MTF) positions decline from record levels. With nearly Rs 72,000 crore exposed to smallcaps, forced liquidations could deepen losses, although SEBI safeguards may limit systemic risks.

items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.
